In various fields, researchers often analyze and compare data sets, and a crucial step in this process involves calculating Kendall's tau, a statistical measure of correlation. A newly designed algorithm can compute Kendall's tau for multiple data points simultaneously, and its computational efficiency increases linearly with the number of observations. This algorithm's effectiveness has been tested on real-world data, and its performance has been compared to a standard method, showing significant improvements in processing time.

The emergence of the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to a significant increase in the number of devices connected to the internet, resulting in a vast amount of data being generated. To address the growing concern over user data security, researchers have developed innovative solutions such as Federated Learning (FL) and Local Differential Privacy (LDP). FL addresses security issues by training models locally on user devices and only transmitting aggregated updates to the central server, whereas LDP ensures data anonymity by applying noise to user data before transmission. Despite these advancements, existing methods have limitations in addressing the security challenges posed by data transmission over unsecured networks. To overcome these limitations, a novel approach called FL-LDP is proposed, which integrates FL and LDP to enhance user data security. The proposed FL-LDP method involves local model training, noisy data generation, and model aggregation, thereby providing robust security for user data. The effectiveness of FL-LDP is demonstrated through experiments conducted on the MNIST dataset, showcasing its superior performance in terms of accuracy and security compared to existing methods.

This study investigates the relationship between the Euler characteristic and more complex invariants in multi-parameter persistent homology through the development of a novel approximation technique. Our approach combines the concepts of interleaving and commutative diagrams to create a more accurate estimation of the multi-parameter topological invariants. To validate our method, we conducted a numerical analysis on a specific dataset derived from the Boolean complex of a 2D grid, and the results demonstrate that our method can significantly reduce the error margin in the estimation of multi-parameter invariants.

This paper explores the application of bifurcation theory in biological population models, with a focus on understanding how changes in parameters can lead to shifts in system behavior. We examine a model that incorporates a time delay and investigate its equilibrium stability through various bifurcation types, including saddle-node, transcritical, Hopf, and singular Hopf bifurcations. We also discuss the potential for complex dynamics to arise from the interaction of multiple equilibria and the possibility of chaotic behavior resulting from Hopf bifurcation.

This study introduces a novel facet pivot approach to the simplex algorithm, which is designed to navigate through the interior of linear programming problem's feasible region. Unlike conventional vertex pivot algorithms, this method can execute an infinite number of steps within a single facet before transitioning to another facet. The new approach is mathematically equivalent to the existing vertex pivot simplex algorithm, but it is capable of solving certain problems more efficiently. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the open-source C++ library, named FacetPivot, which is specifically tailored for this purpose. The implementation includes a proof of concept, which demonstrates the new algorithm's effectiveness in solving certain linear programming problems more efficiently. The FacetPivot library is available for public use on GitHub at the following link: https://github.com/optimization-lab/FacetPivot.

A significant extension of the Quillen–Suslin theory to the realm of graded rings with a group-based grading has been achieved, building upon previous work by Bhatwadekar and Sridharan. This generalization has far-reaching implications in the study of graded rings and their applications in various fields, including the theory of graded rings and their applications in various fields.

This study examines differential top quark pair production cross-sections in proton-proton collisions at the LHC, specifically focusing on the $p$-th order differential distribution $d\hat{\sigma}/d\hat{x}_p$. The analysis is carried out using a next-to-leading-order calculation in QCD, with an emphasis on the transverse momentum of the top quark. The study employs the narrow width approximation and compares results from two different methods of calculating the phase space integral: one using a differential distribution and the other using an integrated approach. The findings indicate that the narrow width approximation can lead to significant discrepancies, with up to 10% differences in the differential distributions. The study also highlights the importance of choosing the correct method of calculation, with an integrated approach being more suitable for certain types of analysis.

This paper presents a novel approach to anti-spoofing detection in facial recognition systems, utilizing transfer learning from vision transformer models. We suggest a simple yet effective method for adapting a pre-trained ViT model to detect spoofing attacks. Our approach involves using a single, lightweight classification head added to the original ViT model, which is then fine-tuned using a relatively small dataset containing images of genuine and spoofed faces. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method using the CASIA-FASD and Replay Attack datasets, where it achieves high accuracy in distinguishing between genuine and spoofed faces. Our results show that the proposed method is capable of achieving state-of-the-art performance in cross-dataset evaluation, where it successfully generalizes to new data not seen during training.

This research paper presents a novel autonomous driving framework that effectively tackles the challenge of making informed decisions in a partially observable environment. The proposed system leverages a combination of a Hidden Markov Model and Recurrent Neural Networks to process and integrate diverse sensor inputs, including visual data from a camera and spatial information from a LiDAR. The integration of these inputs enables the system to accurately predict the location of objects in the driving environment, even in scenarios where visual data is inconclusive. The effectiveness of this framework is demonstrated through a comprehensive evaluation using a large-scale, real-world dataset collected from a self-driving vehicle.

In parallel evolutionary algorithms, a common approach to parent selection involves dividing the population into groups and choosing candidates for reproduction from each group. This method can lead to suboptimal progress in search space exploration. To address this issue, a new parent selection method is proposed, where candidates for reproduction are selected based on interactions between individuals within the same group and those from other groups. This method aims to increase the likelihood of choosing high-fitness individuals as parents, thus improving search progress. The proposed method is evaluated using the OneMax problem and compared to existing algorithms, with results showing its superiority in terms of expected runtime.

This research investigates the spectral bias of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) under the stochastic gradient descent with momentum (SGDM) optimization technique. We demonstrate that SGDM exhibits a spectral bias that favors lower frequencies, and that this phenomenon is amplified by the inertia of the algorithm. Furthermore, we show that the convergence rate of SGDM is contingent upon the initial conditions and is significantly faster than its vanilla counterpart. We also propose a novel PINN architecture that incorporates a learnable inertia parameter, which can be optimized during the training process. We validate the efficacy of this approach through experiments on the Navier-Stokes equations.

This study examines the stability of a wave equation with damping that varies periodically in space and is not smooth, using both Fourier analysis and an energy method. The resulting stability is optimal and depends on the degree of non-smoothness of the damping coefficient. The implications of this non-smoothness on stability and energy decay are further explored through numerical simulations.

Reinforcement learning has been effectively applied to complex decision-making problems, yet its use in safety-critical domains has been hindered by the lack of interpretability. A novel approach to symbolic reinforcement learning is proposed, which can produce a symbolic policy that is both interpretable and provably optimal. This method involves using a symbolic state representation and a first-order logic transition model to define a symbolic goal condition. A customised version of the Dijkstra algorithm is then employed to find a goal-reaching policy, the optimality of which can be formally proven. A new domain, the multi-agent grid world, has been developed to test the applicability of this approach. A comprehensive evaluation of the algorithm's performance and scalability is presented, and the results demonstrate its ability to generate a symbolic policy in a wide range of domains.

We have developed a new, optical-based device that can operate as a full-duplex communication system, utilizing a specific type of inter-resonator interaction that is sensitive to the chirality of the light. This chiral interaction is achieved through a combination of two resonators and a specially designed interaction mechanism that involves a unique inter-resonator coupling. This interaction is characterized by its ability to selectively couple left-handed and right-handed circularly polarized light, which in turn enables the creation of all-optical diodes and quasi-circulators. This device is capable of operating at a wide range of wavelengths and can be tuned to specific frequencies by adjusting the chirality of the light. This device is particularly useful in applications that require high-speed data transmission and can be used in a variety of optical-based systems.

This study investigates the connection between the locations of equioscillation points and optimal configurations, and how they're affected by changes in parameters. We demonstrate that optimal configurations exhibit a form of stability when parameter variations occur, and how this relates to the persistence of equioscillation points. We also explore the implications of this relationship in a specific context, and how it can be used to understand and predict changes in optimal configurations as parameters evolve.

The Dark Matter (DM) interaction with electrons is a crucial area of research, and its detection has been extensively studied. However, previous studies have overlooked the potential of using the $^6$Li isotope in such experiments. In this work, we have developed a comprehensive analytical framework for calculating DM-induced ionization rates in experiments utilizing liquid scintillators and solid-state detectors. By incorporating the effects of $^6$Li, we have found that the resulting sensitivity can be significantly improved, and our findings indicate that experiments such as SNO+ and DRIFT can be highly competitive with other leading DM detection methods.

This study proposes a novel approach to deblurring satellite images captured by consumer-grade cameras, focusing on optimizing the blur kernel structure to achieve the best possible image recovery. The proposed framework involves a two-stage process, where blurring the image is paired with kernel regularization to prevent overfitting. The first stage involves estimating the image and blur kernel using a variational approach, while the second stage involves refining the blur kernel using a novel regularization technique. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance in recovering sharp images from blurred satellite images captured by low-resolution cameras.

In this research, we introduce the concepts of (BiHom-)pre-Lie modules and demonstrate how to construct them from Rota-Baxter (BiHom-)paired modules. We also examine how to construct pre-Lie sections within Lie biHom-2-extensions of Lie biHom-1-terms and show that such sections are equivalent to (1,1)-biHom-cochains in the corresponding cohomology theory.

We have developed a method for automatically verifying imperative programs using assertions expressed in natural language. Our approach combines a natural language parser with a SMT solver to efficiently check the correctness of the code. By leveraging a pre-built dictionary of imperative terms and their corresponding mathematical meanings, we can directly translate these assertions into a format that the SMT solver can process. Our technique is demonstrated through a variety of examples, including a simple sorting algorithm and a more complex image processing function.

This paper introduces RCanopus, an advanced version of the Canopus consensus protocol, designed to enhance resilience against both internal and external attacks. Building on the foundation of leader-based Byzantine agreement protocols, Canopus achieves high performance by achieving linear complexity in terms of message count and communication rounds. However, its reliance on a trusted leader makes it vulnerable to leader failures. To address this limitation, RCanopus incorporates a robust leader election mechanism, ensuring that the protocol can continue to function even in the event of leader failure. By integrating this mechanism, RCanopus achieves linear complexity while providing strong guarantees for both safety and liveness.

The limitations of linear response theory in predicting the behavior of lipid bilayers are highlighted by a comparison of simulation results with experimental data. A discrepancy arises between the linear response theory and experimental findings regarding the relationship between the osmotic modulus and the area compressibility modulus. To resolve this issue, a method is developed that uses simulation data to calculate the area compressibility modulus and the osmotic modulus in a manner that is consistent with equilibrium experiments. This method is validated by applying it to a model lipid bilayer and demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting the behavior of the bilayer under various conditions.

A modified version of the Friedmann equation is derived from loop quantum cosmology by incorporating a specific holonomy correction. This derivation is based on the quantum dynamics of a massless scalar field and the application of a specific Hamiltonian constraint. The modified Friedmann equation is then used to investigate the universe's behavior at high densities, specifically in relation to the loop quantum cosmology model developed by APS. Our analysis reveals that the critical density at which the universe's expansion rate changes from positive to negative is lower in the modified model than in its APS counterpart. Furthermore, we find that the modified model's behavior at high densities is characterized by a smooth transition to a state where the expansion rate decreases, rather than a sudden change as seen in the APS model. Our results also show that the modified model's behavior is consistent with observations of the universe's expansion rate at low densities, suggesting that the modified model may be a viable alternative to the APS model.

A comprehensive catalog of high-energy particles, including 1000 extensive air showers and 10,000 single events, is available for researchers to access. This dataset, collected by the Pierre Auger Observatory between 2004 and 2015, contains events with energies exceeding 10^18 eV, providing a valuable resource for studying the highest-energy particles in the universe.

This paper presents a novel approach for object detection, referred to as BayesOD, which utilizes a Bayesian neural network to predict object detection results, thereby providing a reliable estimate of uncertainty. BayesOD is built upon a standard object detection framework, where a single model generates bounding boxes, class labels, confidence scores, and uncertainty estimates. To achieve this, BayesOD employs a combination of Monte Carlo sampling and a custom loss function, resulting in enhanced accuracy and more effective uncertainty estimation. Experimental results demonstrate that BayesOD surpasses traditional object detection methods in terms of accuracy and uncertainty estimation, with a notable improvement of 1.5% in mean average precision and a 10% reduction in calibration error.

This paper presents a novel traffic forecasting model, F-Net, which leverages a cutting-edge Unet++ architecture to enhance the precision of traffic prediction. The Unet++ design allows the model to effectively combine high-level spatial context with detailed traffic patterns, thereby improving its predictive capabilities. The model's performance was rigorously evaluated using a comprehensive dataset of hourly traffic counts from 1,000 locations in London, collected over a 12-month period. The experimental results demonstrate that F-Net surpasses existing state-of-the-art forecasting methods, with a notable 10% improvement in accuracy.

We establish the conditions under which a specific type of rewriting system operates efficiently and consistently in the context of precategories, and we demonstrate the practical application of these conditions to model category theory and algebraic topology.

Current deep learning-based hippocampus segmentation methods are primarily trained on healthy individuals and may struggle to accurately segment hippocampi from patients who have undergone a surgical resection. This study evaluates the performance of state-of-the-art hippocampus segmentation models on both healthy and post-resection hippocampi, revealing that these models are unable to accurately segment the resected tissue. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that involves training a U-Net model on a dataset containing synthetic resections, and we demonstrate that this method can accurately segment hippocampi from patients who have undergone a surgical resection.

The relationship between path and traversal information in double-slit experiments is examined, with a focus on how it can be modified by the transverse modes of photons. It is found that the correlation between path and traversal degrees of freedom is not absolute, but can be manipulated by selecting specific modes. This effect is particularly pronounced in experiments involving photons generated through spontaneous parametric down-conversion, where path and traversal correlations are found to be maximally anti-correlated in certain modes. Moreover, the study reveals that the path-traversal complementarity can be optimized by choosing specific modes, and that this optimization is linked to the mode-dependent traversal wavefunction.

The origin of protons in Earth's atmosphere is a result of high-energy cosmic ray collisions, which produce protons that can be detected by specialized instruments. A new experiment, called ATIC-III, has been designed to detect these low flux protons with high precision by utilizing a unique combination of a balloon-borne detector and a specially engineered target. This experiment aims to measure the flux of protons with energies between 10 and 100 GeV with a precision of 10% by collecting a large number of protons over a period of 100 days. A comprehensive simulation of the ATIC-III detector has been conducted to assess its performance and potential for measuring the flux of protons with the desired precision.

The proposed framework employs a hierarchical structure, where each layer is linked to the one above it, and information flows in both directions. The proposed framework was tested on a range of tasks, including image classification, and the results show that it outperforms traditional methods in both training efficiency and generalization. The proposed framework was also found to be effective in other tasks, including image segmentation and object detection.

This study introduces a novel randomized mechanism, the Huber mechanism, which combines elements from both the Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms. The performance of this new mechanism is evaluated in terms of its differential privacy and utility. The results show that the Huber mechanism outperforms the Laplace mechanism and is comparable to the Gaussian mechanism.

The Most Clicks Problem (MCP) involves finding the maximum number of times a mouse can click on an $m \times n$ grid, where each click must be on a cell that hasn't been clicked in the current row or column. This study demonstrates that the maximum number of clicks is equal to the grid's nullity, which is determined by the number of times the mouse can click on a single cell without restriction. A recursive algorithm is presented to solve the MCP, and it is shown that the maximum number of clicks is equal to the minimum of the grid's dimensions.

This research introduces a novel approach to adapting the piecewise constant Mumford-Shah model for segmenting degraded images. We present a discrete model that incorporates a data fidelity term to account for non-linear image distortions. To handle this, we utilize a nonlinear filtering process to clean up the image data. We also incorporate a novel total variation term to handle the gradient penalty, which is formulated as a non-linear optimization problem. We demonstrate the model's convergence in the context of Sobolev spaces and develop an efficient algorithm to solve the resulting optimization problem. We validate our approach through a series of numerical experiments.

Static program analysis techniques, particularly abstract interpretation, can be greatly enhanced by abstracting program states to reduce complexity. A key challenge in this process is minimizing over-approximations in the interpreter to avoid overly broad results. This paper introduces a novel approach to abstracting program states, which enables the creation of a more accurate and efficient interpreter. The proposed method leverages a program's control flow graph to create a more refined approximation of program states, thereby improving the accuracy of the analysis. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through a concrete example, which shows that incorporating program flow can significantly reduce complexity in the analysis.

Perovskite crystals in a tetragonal phase are known to host topological phonons, 
yet it's unclear how photoexcitation affects their emergence. Our research reveals 
that a photoexcitation-induced modification of the crystal structure can create 
conditions for topological phonons to emerge. Specifically, we studied how 
exciting a non-interacting phonon mode in a model of barium titanate can induce 
a phase transition to a topological phonon crystal. Our findings show that 
exciting this mode can cause the crystal to transition into a topological phonon 
crystal, characterized by a change in the phonon band gap and the appearance 
of edge modes. Our work demonstrates that photoexcitation can be used to control 
the topological properties of phononic crystals.

In outlier detection research, the proximity graph used significantly affects performance.  A proposed modified proximity graph, termed MRPG, is designed to enhance outlier detection efficiency by reducing the number of edges in the graph.  This new graph is based on a modified rule that considers the density of the data points, and is shown to produce fewer edges than the minimum spanning tree and the uniform minimum spanning graph.  A new metric, termed the outlier detection efficiency, is introduced to evaluate the performance of the proposed graph.  This metric is defined as the ratio of the number of edges in the MRPG to the total number of data points.  A theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed metric is lower than that of the minimum spanning tree and the uniform minimum spanning graph.  A comprehensive simulation study is conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed graph in outlier detection.  The results show that the proposed graph consistently produces fewer false positives and false negatives than the minimum spanning tree and the uniform minimum spanning graph.  A real-world application of the proposed graph is demonstrated using a dataset from the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

We investigate the dynamics of a two-level atom moving at a constant speed in a vacuum that contains a stationary, perfectly reflective mirror. The atom's motion is analyzed in a specific frame where it remains at a constant distance from the mirror. We derive an analytical solution for the emission rate of photons by the atom and find that it is influenced by both the atom's motion and its distance from the mirror. We also examine the conditions under which the emission rate is maximized and discuss the implications of these findings.

Recent research has highlighted the importance of incorporating fairness into graph representation learning. However, many existing methods focus solely on achieving neighborhood equity without considering the impact on the learned representations. This study proposes a novel approach, the Fair Graph Autoencoder (FGAE), which enforces fairness constraints during the learning process to produce equitable graph representations. The FGAE framework employs a dual autoencoder architecture, where the primary autoencoder generates graph node embeddings, and the secondary autoencoder ensures that these nodes are mapped to a fair latent space. The FGAE framework is evaluated on a variety of real-world datasets and tasks, demonstrating its ability to improve both fairness and accuracy. The FGAE framework outperforms existing methods in terms of link prediction accuracy and also achieves better fairness metrics. The FGAE framework is shown to be versatile and applicable to a range of graph tasks, including node classification and community detection. The FGAE framework is made available on the GitHub repository: https://github.com/yourusername/FGAE.

The conventional Michaelis-Menten model, which is widely used to analyze enzyme kinetics, is an approximation that can be improved by applying more accurate methods. In this study, we apply the Homotopy Perturbation Method (HPM) and the Simple Iteration Method (SIM) to derive precise solutions for reversible enzyme reaction models. These refined solutions are then compared to the traditional Michaelis-Menten model, revealing that the HPM and SIM methods yield results that align more closely with actual experimental data.

We've conducted a search for long-lived gluinos at the LHC, utilizing data collected by the CMS experiment in 2016. The data, totaling 13 TeV and 35.9 fb$^{-1}$ in luminosity, was analyzed to identify events with displaced jets and at least one unassociated jet. The analysis found no evidence of gluino production beyond the Standard Model, setting new limits on the mass and decay length of long-lived gluinos. The results show that this search is more sensitive than traditional searches for long-lived particles, particularly for gluino decay lengths between 1 and 100 cm, where it can exclude masses up to 1.1 TeV for a 10 cm decay length. The results are also compared to other searches, demonstrating the CMS's search's unique sensitivity in this parameter space.

Financial markets often experience bubble-like price fluctuations, which are characterized by rapid price increases followed by sudden crashes. This study employs a mathematical model to examine the dynamics of bubbles in a market of agents with diverse investment strategies. The model reveals that a market's collective behavior is influenced by a nonlinear feedback mechanism, which can lead to the amplification of small price changes and their eventual collapse. The model's findings suggest that a market's positive feedback can cause a bubble to grow, but it is inevitably followed by a crash due to the reversal of this feedback mechanism. The model's implications are further explored in the context of real-world financial data, which reveals that a market's dynamics can be accurately predicted by a simple mathematical equation.

In the context of a driven quantum system, we explore the possibility of generating coherent states by interacting with a specific type of wave, characterized by a constant curvature in space. The analysis is based on a simplified model that involves a two-level system and a wave, described by a specific mathematical equation. The model is then extended to a more complex scenario, involving a two-level system and a wave with multiple energy levels. The conditions under which coherent states can be generated are derived, and it is found that they can occur in both the original and the more complex models. The model also has potential applications in the study of light-matter interactions and the development of new technologies in the field of quantum information.

This research introduces a novel model that leverages interactions within reviews to predict item recommendations. The model, known as Interactive Rating, integrates review content and interactions to forecast users' ratings. The Interactive Rating model is composed of two interconnected modules: one that analyzes review content using a multi-layer perceptron and another that captures review interactions using a multi-layer perceptron. The two modules' outputs are combined to produce a rating score, which is then used to calculate user preferences through a factorization machine. The model's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of experiments on a large dataset, which reveal that review interactions significantly impact the final rating score. The model's performance is further validated by its ability to outperform baseline models in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.

This paper presents a method for generating high-quality code-switching data by replacing segments within sentences, rather than entire words. The proposed approach utilizes a sequence-to-sequence model with attention mechanisms to create parallel data for multiple languages. The revised method outperforms the existing technique by producing more natural code-switching data, as evidenced by a significant 10.5% improvement in a quality evaluation task.

Let $G$ be a subgroup of the homeomorphism group of a compact surface $X$, with its interior denoted as $X^\circ$. The interior's homeomorphism group is represented by $G^\circ$. The text proves that if $G^\circ$ acts transitively on $X^\circ$, then $G^\circ$ is precompact.

We have developed a method to create holographic duals for brane setups that transition between different fixed points in the ultraviolet and infrared regions. By embedding these branes in a specific type of warped space that smoothly connects these two fixed points, we can study the behavior of the corresponding field theory under renormalization group transformations. Our analysis focuses on two types of setups: one involving a stack of D5-branes and the other consisting of a combination of D3 and D5 branes. We have calculated the properties of the warped spaces in the ultraviolet and infrared limits and found that the behavior of the space changes significantly as the transition occurs. We have also determined the critical value of a parameter that marks the point at which the transition occurs.

The quality of mesh elements significantly impacts the accuracy of computed results, and a reliable method for evaluating mesh quality is crucial for this purpose. A new metric has been developed for unstructured meshes, and its effectiveness is demonstrated through comparisons with established quality measures.

This paper examines the connection between knowledge graph link prediction and
relation extraction, exploring how the latter can enhance the former. We propose
a method for using trained relation extraction models to improve link prediction
performance. Our experiments on the Wikipedia KG demonstrate that incorporating
pre-trained relation extraction models yields better results than using only
link prediction models.

This paper introduces an innovative analytical delay model for CMOS inverters, which is based on a straightforward analytical voltage source model and a constant resistance approximation. The proposed model is evaluated against SPICE simulations and experimental results, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy. Specifically, the model achieves a substantial reduction in delay estimation error, ranging from 10% to 15%, compared to the traditional approach. Furthermore, the model exhibits minimal sensitivity to process variations, resulting in a minimal error rate of approximately 1% in the face of such fluctuations.

Deep reinforcement learning has made significant advancements in recent years, yet it still faces several unresolved issues. One of the key challenges is the lack of a clear understanding of the underlying principles that make deep RL methods effective. To address this, we propose a novel approach to define the smoothness of a function in a more general setting, specifically for continuous state-action spaces. Our definition builds upon previous work on smoothness in tabular domains and incorporates concepts from differential geometry. We demonstrate the practical applications of our smoothness definition in two key areas: function approximation and data augmentation. Function approximation is used to enhance the learning process by leveraging the smoothness of the value function, while data augmentation is used to expand the available training data by exploiting the smoothness of the environment's transition dynamics. Our experiments show that these techniques significantly improve the performance of deep RL methods, particularly in complex environments like the half-cheat box domain.

Our research examines the concept of animacy as a continuous spectrum, rather than a binary classification. To this end, we developed the animacy space model, which utilizes multidimensional scaling to position various entities on a continuum based on their animacy ratings. Our analysis of the animacy space reveals that two distinct factors, visual categorizability and autonomy, contribute to animacy in separate dimensions. Our findings suggest that categorizability and autonomy are independent factors that can be used to position entities on the animacy spectrum. Our model also highlights the importance of considering both human and non-human entities in the context of animacy, and provides a framework for further research on the concept.

This study introduces a novel family of structure-preserving filters, which are designed to rectify inconsistencies in PDE simulations based on polynomials. Unlike conventional filtering methods, this approach not only eliminates spurious oscillations but also preserves the continuous system's inherent structures. The filter is formulated as a polynomial function that operates on the discrete solution, yielding another discrete solution. By applying the filter to the Discontinuous Galerkin method for the linear advection equation, we demonstrate its efficacy in eliminating inconsistencies and preserving key structures. Furthermore, we establish a theoretical framework for the filtered DG method, which reveals its equivalence to a Riemann solver-based DG scheme.

We conducted an in-depth analysis of the type-C QPOs observed in the black hole X-ray transient GX 339-4, focusing on the data collected by the NuSTAR and IXPE telescopes. Our findings indicate that type-C QPOs occur exclusively during the hard-intermediate state, with a frequency range of 0.1-1.5 Hz. We discovered that the QPO frequency increases with increasing hard X-ray flux, and the X-ray spectrum becomes harder as the QPO frequency increases. Our analysis of the polarization angle revealed a significant increase in the polarization angle during the presence of type-C QPOs, and we observed a positive correlation between the polarization angle and the QPO frequency. Our results suggest that the QPOs are generated in the vicinity of the inner edge of the accretion disk, and the polarization angle variations are caused by the changing orientation of the accretion disk's magnetic field.

This paper introduces a novel method for enhancing the capabilities of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) through the application of transfer empowerment. We utilize a multi-objective reinforcement learning approach to achieve both increased empowerment and improved task performance. The proposed method leverages a novel multi-objective empowerment metric, which enables the simultaneous consideration of multiple factors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach using a simulated four-wheeled robot navigation task and a real-world two-agent MARL scenario.

Our approach to one-shot learning enables the recognition of unknown materials under various circumstances. We utilize a single image of an object to extract a latent representation, which is then used to generate a material-specific renderer. This system can then create a virtual view of the object from any angle. We evaluate our method using a combination of real-world and synthetic datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in both controlled and real-world settings.

This study explores the cohomology theory of Lie 2-algebras, specifically focusing on cohomology in degrees 1 through 5. The research also examines the cohomology of Lie 2-algebras with values in cochain 2-modules, with an emphasis on the 3-cocycle condition. The study establishes connections to Lie 3-algebras and examines cohomology in degree 4 and 5, revealing relationships to Lie 4-algebras.

This paper presents a novel approach to image registration that circumvents conventional image feature detection and matching techniques. Instead, it leverages a neural network to identify corresponding features across images, thereby enhancing registration accuracy. The proposed method employs a self-supervised learning framework, allowing the network to be trained without labeled data. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through experiments on various datasets, showcasing its superiority over existing methods.

The accuracy of magnetic field maps derived from vector magnetograms is heavily influenced by the assumption that magnetic fields are uniformly distributed across a pixel. However, this assumption is often flawed, as magnetic fields are not always evenly distributed. To address this issue, we developed a method to account for the uneven distribution of magnetic fields by incorporating magnetic fill fraction into the inversion process. By comparing our new method to the standard uniform distribution approach, we found that our method yields more accurate results, as evidenced by the reduced error in the magnetic field measurements. Furthermore, we found that our method yields more accurate results when applied to simulated data that mimics real solar conditions. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, we applied it to a real solar observation and found that our method yields more accurate results than the standard uniform distribution approach.

This study examines a real-time pricing system where a central unit isn't necessarily present, and consumers negotiate pricing agreements with the system operator through the operator broadcasts a price. The operator aims to minimize its energy consumption costs by setting a price, while consumers seek to maximize their savings by choosing contracts that result in optimal consumption schedules. The proposed model involves an iterative process where the operator adjusts its price based on a best response strategy, and consumers update their contracts accordingly. The model demonstrates that under specific conditions, the system converges to a stable state, and numerical simulations confirm this outcome.

In this study, we examine the quantum stability of charged black strings within the framework of quantum gravity, specifically focusing on the influence of quantum gravity effects on the system's stability. We derive a set of master equations that describe the quantum fluctuations of the black string, and then analyze their impact on the string's stability. Our results show that quantum gravity effects can significantly alter the stability conditions of charged black strings, and that the string's quantum fluctuations can lead to a more complex stability behavior. We also investigate the impact of these quantum fluctuations on the black string's horizon and find that they can cause the string to become unstable in certain parameter ranges. Our findings have important implications for our understanding of quantum gravity and its potential effects on astrophysical systems.

This study examines the connection between two key aspects of the Ergodic Theorem by von Neumann. Firstly, it investigates the rate of convergence for time-averages in the absence of a spectral gap, and relates this rate to the rate of convergence for Cesaro means in a related operator sequence. Secondly, it establishes a connection between the rate of convergence for time-averages and the rate of convergence for the mean values of a specific operator sequence. The results are demonstrated using a combination of techniques, including interpolation, and have implications for the Riesz theorem on the convergence of Fourier series.

The iron abundance of stars is a crucial factor in understanding their characteristics, yet it's often difficult to measure precisely. We've developed a method to estimate a star's iron content based on the ratio of specific spectral features, which can be easily calculated from low-resolution spectra. By applying this method to a dataset of stars with known iron abundance, we found that it can accurately predict iron abundance with a margin of error of approximately 0.1 dex. Furthermore, we've discovered that this method can effectively classify stars into metal-rich, metal-poor, and solar metallicity categories with a high degree of accuracy. We've also applied this method to a dataset of M-dwarfs and found that it can accurately estimate their iron abundance.

This study examines the spatial and temporal patterns of the 2019-2020 Australian bushfires, analyzing daily fire counts across the continent. By mapping daily fire counts to a grid system, we identify trends in fire activity and their relationship with temperature and rainfall. Our analysis reveals that certain areas experienced rising fire numbers during the season, while others saw declining numbers. Furthermore, we found that temperature and rainfall significantly influenced fire activity, with higher temperatures and lower rainfall correlating with increased fire numbers.

This research explores the connections between the inherent intricacy of word forms and fundamental aspects of language classification. To investigate this, we examine the relationships between the structural complexity of word forms and key variables such as word order, affixation, and morphophonemic patterns. We utilize a unique approach by analyzing the syntactic and phonetic structure of word forms through a visual representation, allowing us to compare the inherent complexity of word forms across different languages. We then assess the relationships between the structural features of these word forms and the three typological variables in a statistical framework. Our results indicate that the structural features of word forms are significantly linked to word order, agglutinative vs. fusional patterns, and morphophonemic irregularity. We also find that the structural features of word forms are not significantly linked to the degree of SOV vs. SVO variation.

A widely used technique for efficiently solving PDEs with uncertain parameters involves choosing a suitable reduction basis. The effectiveness of this method heavily relies on the observation operator, which is often chosen based on the sensitivities of specific parameters. However, this approach can be problematic when the sensitivity profiles of different parameters vary significantly. In this study, we propose a novel method for choosing the observation operator by considering the entire parameter space. The proposed method involves using the adjoint of the forward reduced model to iteratively improve the reduction basis. The results show that this approach can lead to more accurate solutions and faster convergence rates.

Dimensionality reduction techniques have been developed to address the issue of high-dimensional data. A novel approach, m-arithmetic-geometric-Kullback-Leibler divergence, has been proposed to further reduce dimensionality. This new method combines the Kullback-Leibral divergence with the arithmetic-geometric mean, offering a more efficient way to perform dimensionality reduction. A novel feature extraction technique, based on the proposed divergence, has been developed and its performance evaluated. A comparison with existing feature extraction methods revealed that the proposed technique outperforms them in terms of feature quality and dimensionality reduction efficiency.

This paper introduces a groundbreaking spatio-temporal event detection system that leverages the inherent properties of events to identify and locate occurrences with precise spatial and temporal localization. The proposed system addresses the challenge of events with varying spatial dimensions by representing events as point processes and employing a novel kernel function that accommodates these dimensions. By utilizing a maximum likelihood estimation approach, the system can accurately predict the spatial and temporal localization of events. The efficacy of the proposed system is demonstrated through its application to predicting the spread of COVID-19 cases in the United States.

This paper explores the properties of A-harmonic functions in connection with free boundary problems in elliptic equations, with a particular focus on the Laplacian. We establish the Hausdorff dimension of the free boundary in a manner that does not rely on dimensional analysis, and we demonstrate that this boundary is relatively open. Our approach is applicable to a broader class of equations, including those with coefficients that are measurable and bounded.

This study examines the magnetic properties of YCo and Y$_{2}$Co$_{17}$ compounds, which are part of the YCo$_{n}$ series. The compounds were synthesized using the arc-melting method and their crystal structures were confirmed through X-ray diffraction. The magnetic properties were evaluated using SQUID magnetometry, which revealed that YCo and Y$_{2}$Co$_{17}$ exhibit higher magnetization and Curie temperatures than Y$_{2}$Co$_{14}$. The compounds exhibit ferromagnetic behavior at room temperature, and their magnetic properties can be attributed to the magnetic moments of Co ions. The magnetic moments of YCo and Y$_{2}$Co$_{17}$ are 1.58 $\mu_{B}$/Co and 1.45 $\mu_{B}$/Co, respectively. The compounds exhibit a high saturation magnetization, which is desirable for their potential use in magnetic applications.

A proposed method for generating bidding algorithms from predefined knowledge is capable of adapting to individual preferences, and it is formulated in a way that is both interpretable and verifiable. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through a comprehensive analysis of its capabilities, and its performance is validated through a thorough evaluation of its ability to adapt to various risk tendencies. The results show that the method's generated algorithms outperform those created using alternative methods, and it is particularly adept at adapting to a wide range of risk levels.

We've found that two parties can create a Wigner negative state in one of their systems, even if they're not directly connected through quantum correlations. This happens when they share a non-Gaussian state and use a specific process to split it up. Our research shows that for certain types of states, the quantum correlations required to create the non-Gaussian effects can be completely removed. This means the non-Gaussianity of the state is what's responsible for creating the Wigner negative state, rather than the quantum correlations. Our findings have implications for using the Wigner negativity as an indicator of quantum correlations.

In the context of quantum key distribution, we investigate the impact of imperfect random number generation on the secure key rate. Our analysis reveals that the average min-entropy of the generator directly influences the secure bound, and we derive a general formula for the key rate in the presence of random number generation errors. This formula is then applied to a specific protocol, the BB84 protocol, and we obtain an explicit expression for the key rate in the presence of random number generation errors. Our findings also highlight the importance of using high-quality random number generators in practical quantum key distribution systems.

This research paper examines the concept of Bertrand curves within the context of three-dimensional Euclidean space and its various subspaces, including the Euclidean, Minkowski, and de Sitter spaces, as well as the Minkowski and lightcone subspaces. By exploring these different spaces, the study aims to identify and analyze specific types of Bertrand curves, such as de Sitter, Minkowski, and de Sitter curves, as well as certain special cases like null curves. The results of this investigation reveal that the notion of a Bertrand curve is well-defined in both the Euclidean and de Sitter spaces, whereas it is not applicable in the Minkowski space.

We've developed a mathematical framework for the evolution of a population experiencing spatially varying selection pressures. This framework is based on a stochastic model that involves multiple types of population, each with distinct traits and characteristics. The model we've developed is particularly suited to studying the effects of spatially heterogeneous environments on the diffusion of mutations. We've shown that under certain conditions, the model can be simplified to a deterministic equation that describes the average behavior of the population. This equation can be used to study the effects of different types of selection pressures on the evolution of the population. We've also investigated the behavior of the model in the limit of small noise and found that it can be used to study the effects of different types of selection pressures on the evolution of the population.

This research investigates the impact of quantum feedback on single-qubit waveguide QED systems, focusing on coherent feedback using beam splitters and phase shifters. We demonstrate that delayed coherent quantum feedback can transform qubit scattering matrices, allowing for a broader range of N-photon scattering matrix parametrizations. We also show that this effect can be applied to create non-Clifford gates, specifically the T gate, and that it can be used to create multi-photon Fock states with high fidelity.

We investigate the detection of sub-GeV spin-dependent boosted dark matter through its impact on polarized electrons in fixed-target experiments. By utilizing data from LUXE, PAO, and JLab's MAMI, we establish a benchmark for special interactions over conventional methods. Our analysis reveals that LUXE's sensitivity to this particular interaction surpasses that of conventional contact interactions by a factor of 100. Furthermore, we compare the LUXE sensitivity to existing and proposed spin-dependent searches, including those conducted by XENONnT, LZ, and DUNE.

The connection between Faulhaber's formula and Bernoulli numbers is well-established,
yet a deeper understanding of this relationship can be achieved by viewing Faulhaber's
formula as a means to compute Bernoulli numbers through summing powers.
This paper presents an algorithm that utilizes Faulhaber's formula to calculate
Bernoulli numbers and demonstrates its computational efficiency, particularly in
large-scale computations, by leveraging parallel processing capabilities.

This research introduces a new method for non-coherent differential detection of continuous phase modulation signals, achieving better performance than the traditional technique and approaching the optimal results seen in coherent detection methods. The novel detection scheme is implemented using a continuous-time approach, thereby reducing the bit error rate by roughly two orders of magnitude compared to the traditional method.

Human feedback is a crucial component in reward learning, yet it can be costly and time-consuming. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach that leverages batch processing of comparisons to optimize the process. By presenting multiple comparisons simultaneously, we can gather feedback more efficiently, and our method's effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments on both synthetic and real-world tasks, where it outperforms existing sequential methods.

A noncommutative phase space theory is proposed to address inconsistencies between theoretical and experimental data for nucleon structure functions at low Bjorken x values. The theory's noncommutativity correction significantly reduces the discrepancy, aligning theoretical and experimental data within a factor of 1.5. Furthermore, the theory's parameters are found to be consistent with those derived from other independent methods.

The interplay between frustration and nonlinearity in quantum systems can lead to fascinating phenomena, such as the emergence of topological order. In this study, we investigate the non-linear quantum Heisenberg model with a toroidal geometry, where we find that the non-linearity can be viewed as a type of frustration, resulting in a rich and diverse phase diagram. Notably, we find that the system exhibits a unique phase characterized by a non-trivial topological order, where we identify a set of local operators that can be used to describe the system's ground state. Our findings suggest that the system's phase diagram is highly sensitive to the model's parameters, and that the emergence of topological order is associated with a specific type of frustration. Our results provide new insights into the behavior of quantum systems and may have implications for the development of quantum technologies.

We investigate the complex eigenvalue distribution of a specific type of random Hermitian matrix, which is composed of independent, zero-mean Gaussian entries. The matrix's diagonal elements have a distinct variance, denoted as $\sigma^2$, and we examine the eigenvalue distribution in the limit as the matrix's size approaches infinity. Our analysis reveals that the eigenvalue distribution is influenced by the relative magnitude of the variance parameter $\sigma$ and the size of the matrix. Specifically, when $\sigma$ is significantly larger than 1, the distribution converges to a specific mathematical function, whereas for smaller values of $\sigma$, the distribution exhibits a more intricate structure characterized by an infinite series of complex poles.

This paper presents a novel task of identifying semantic connections between dialogue utterances, a crucial aspect of dialogue comprehension. We introduce the SemDist dataset, comprising 1.1 million annotated dialogue pairs from the Reddit Daily Dialogue corpus, and establish a graph-based representation to capture the relationships between dialogue statements. We compare multiple deep learning approaches, including relation prediction and representation learning, and find that incorporating utterance semantics and dialogue context enhances performance. The SemDist dataset is available on GitHub at https://github.com/joyiee/SemDist.

As machine learning algorithms become increasingly complex, their opacity poses a significant challenge to their trustworthiness. To address this issue, researchers have developed techniques for interpreting their behavior, but these methods are often limited to specific models and lack generalizability. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel approach for interpreting algorithms through a framework that allows for the analysis of their behavior across various domains. Our method, which is grounded in information theory, provides a comprehensive understanding of how algorithms function by identifying and explaining their internal components. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by applying it to a wide range of algorithms and tasks, including image classification, and showcase its potential to uncover novel insights into algorithm behavior.

Anomaly detection is a critical area of research within data mining, and the Isolation Forest algorithm has emerged as a prominent solution. This paper presents an anomaly detection method based on Isolation Forest, which is designed to identify irregularities in data by creating isolation trees. The algorithm's effectiveness is evaluated through a series of experiments, which demonstrate its ability to accurately detect anomalies in various real-world datasets. The results of these experiments reveal that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

This paper introduces a Bayesian model for analyzing extreme values, where the choice of a key parameter m significantly impacts estimation. We explore the implications of this factor and propose a method to determine it. Our approach involves using a Bayesian model with a prior distribution for the parameter a, and we demonstrate that this model effectively captures the behavior of extreme values. We also discuss the relationship between this model and the Pickands-Balkema-Embrechts theorem, and provide evidence that this model is consistent with empirical data.

The unique characteristics of stationary forms in the context of the curvature flow are investigated in 3-dimensional space, focusing on the stability of self-shrinkers and their implications for nearby shapes.

We introduce ATOMIC 2020, an expansive set of 100 million cause-and-effect relationships annotated by humans, designed to aid in the development of common sense knowledge models. This dataset surpasses existing resources in size and diversity, encompassing knowledge about 100,000 human-related entities and 10,000 event types. Our evaluation of the state-of-the-art models reveals that the leading models struggle to accurately predict cause-and-effect relationships, achieving an average accuracy of 30.5%. In contrast, the best-performing models based on our dataset attain an average accuracy of 50.0%, outperforming the existing state-of-the-art.

This paper outlines the key components of the Hi-GAL survey's data processing pipeline, detailing the procedures used to enhance data quality and reduce noise. The system is designed to accommodate a variety of data types, including those from the Spitzer Space Telescope and the Herschel Space Observatory. The data processing pipeline is built using the Python language and the IRSA Data Models Language, allowing for efficient handling of the large datasets generated by the Hi-GAL survey. The paper also provides a comprehensive overview of the data processing pipeline, including the steps taken to identify and correct for instrumental effects, and the methods used to optimize the data quality.

Spectroscopic data from the UV to the IR range revealed the abundances of 18 elements in these stars. The results show that the outer regions of NGC 6441 contain stars with chemical compositions similar to those in the inner regions, with the exception of Na, Al, and Ca. The accuracy-speed relationship in one-dimensional systems is examined through the lens of the means square displacement. This is applied to a variety of models, including those with different movement patterns and a system that mimics the movement of a single particle in a confined space. The analysis reveals that the accuracy-speed relationship is significantly influenced by the type of movement pattern and the system's spatial constraints.

The recent Frauchiger-Renner and Hardy's paradoxes have generated significant controversy in quantum foundations. In this paper, we propose a quantum version of Bayes' rule that effectively resolves the paradoxes presented by Frauchiger-Renner and Hardy's setups.

This research examines the impact of periodic boundary conditions on the asymptotic behavior of quantum field theories in 1+1 dimensions. It is found that the influence of periodic boundary conditions is more pronounced than that of Dirichlet boundary conditions, which aligns with the understanding that they introduce a more confined system. Furthermore, the study investigates the effect of a specific type of boundary condition, known as Robin, and discovers that it can lead to a distinct asymptotic behavior. It is also demonstrated that the transition between different boundary conditions can be continuous, which implies that the choice of boundary conditions may not have a significant impact on the overall behavior of the system.

Building upon the work of Miller, Miller-Rothenberg and others, we have established the existence of a non-zero algebraic transmission from $H^{*}(C_{p};\mathcal{A})$ to $H^{*}(BP;\mathcal{A})$ at the prime 2 for a specific value of $n=5$. This transmission is shown to contain several key elements, such as $x_{12,16}$, $x_{14,20}$, $x_{16,24}$, $x_{16,26}$ and $x_{20,32}$. Our findings also indicate that certain elements, including $x_{12,16}$, $x_{14,20}$, $x_{16,24}$ and $x_{20,32}$, were previously undetected. In addition, we have established the existence of non-zero transmissions for $n=4$ at the prime 3 and for $n=5$ at the prime 5.

A high-pressure cell filled with molecular hydrogen is used to filter out Lyman-alpha photons from a beam of light. The effectiveness of this filter is evaluated by measuring the transmission rate of the light as a function of the hydrogen pressure. The experiment is conducted by comparing the intensity of a Lyman-alpha photon source with and without the filter in place. The results show that the transmission rate of the light is in agreement with a theoretical model that takes into account the self-broadening of the light due to collisions with hydrogen molecules. The model also includes the effect of the light's polarization and the Doppler shift of the photon source. The experiment is repeated for different hydrogen pressures and the results are in good agreement with the theoretical model. The results show that the transmission rate of the light is maximized when the light is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The experiment is repeated for different magnetic field strengths and the results show that the transmission rate of the light is in agreement with a theoretical model that takes into account the Zeeman splitting of the hydrogen energy levels. The transmission rate of the light is also measured as a function of the temperature of the hydrogen gas in the absorption cell. The results show that the transmission rate of the light is maximized when the temperature is low. This paper addresses the challenge of balancing communication costs and performance in distributed control systems. A novel approach is proposed, where a central controller manages a network of interconnected subsystems, each with its own performance optimization goals. To minimize communication overhead, a new method is developed to determine the optimal amount of data to transmit from the subsystems to the controller. The proposed method involves designing a variable selection mechanism that ensures the communication links between the subsystems and the controller are efficient. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this approach can achieve the same performance as if all data were transmitted. A numerical example is provided to validate the proposed method.

This study presents a novel approach to detecting images on the web using active indexing, which enhances the resilience of the method by employing diverse image transformations. The proposed framework, which is built upon the concept of active indexing, incorporates a new image transformation strategy called the adaptive Gaussian filter. This technique selectively smooths areas of an image that are not critical to its overall content, thereby preserving the integrity of the image's key features. The experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms the existing state-of-the-art techniques in both accuracy and efficiency.

This study examines the feasibility of securely modifying a code used for a memoryless channel, where the original code was designed for maximum data transmission efficiency without considering security. The modified code maintains the same asymptotically negligible transmission rate but is intended to withstand an adversary attempting to forge messages using a limited amount of information. The proposed solution involves a two-step process: first, a legitimate user encodes the message using the original code; second, a limited number of information bits are transmitted to the receiver, which are used to narrow down the possible message options. The results show that this approach can achieve a level of security comparable to the data transmission rate itself, which is a significant improvement over previous methods.

Our research examines the long-term movement of Brownian particles in a periodically changing environment with a specific type of potential and time-varying friction. By analyzing the system's dynamics, we found that it can be effectively simplified to a single-variable model. This model reveals that the system exhibits superdiffusion behavior, characterized by a specific exponent of 1.4. This superdiffusion behavior persists even when the system is far from equilibrium, and it remains relatively stable across a range of system parameters.

This study examines the economic repercussions of sudden financial disruptions using a comprehensive model that integrates financial and real sectors. Our findings indicate that the impact of these disruptions on the economy is contingent upon their magnitude and direction, with the potential to either stimulate or depress economic activity. Furthermore, we observe that the effects of sudden financial disruptions are short-lived, with the potential to generate amplified fluctuations in the economy that are disproportionate to the initial shock.

In a strong magnetic field, an electron's motion is confined to Landau levels, 
and its orbital and spin movements are tightly coupled. 
When the electron's motion is perturbed, 
recoil from emitted photons can cause it to transition to higher Landau levels. 
Our research reveals that the recoil from vacuum photons increases with the electron's 
kinetic angular momentum, 
while the recoil from a strong magnetic field decreases with it. 
This implies that the electron's angular momentum is transferred to the magnetic field, 
resulting in a change in the magnetic field's polarization. 
This phenomenon is known as the vacuum Zeeman effect, 
and it can be observed in the polarization of light emitted by the electron.

This paper presents the FGNET-RH framework, a method for enhancing entity classification within a social media context. The framework utilizes a knowledge graph to capture entity relationships and a Twitter dataset to improve type representation. The framework's approach involves incorporating relationship context into entity encoding through the integration of a knowledge graph and a social network graph. The framework's efficacy is demonstrated through a state-of-the-art performance on a social media dataset, outperforming previous methods by a significant margin.

We establish initial findings for specific $\eta$-univalent function classes within the open unit disk, define these function classes, and derive $\eta$-univalent function estimates along with inequalities of Wendland type.

The widespread adoption of virtualization has made cloud computing a viable option for businesses seeking to reduce costs and increase efficiency. Cloud providers can now offer services on demand, allowing users to scale resources as needed. However, managing the scheduling of virtual machines (VMs) in a cloud environment poses a significant challenge, particularly when it comes to optimizing resource allocation and minimizing energy consumption. To address this issue, a new approach called Prepartition has been developed, which allows for more efficient resource allocation and improved scheduling outcomes. By pre-allocating resources to potential VM hosts, Prepartition enables the scheduler to make more informed decisions and achieve better overall performance. Experimental results demonstrate that Prepartition outperforms existing scheduling methods, particularly in scenarios involving resource over-subscription.

Game theory is a powerful tool for modeling complex interactions between multiple agents, and predicting the equilibrium of a game is crucial for determining the final outcome. However, the task of predicting the equilibrium of a game is extremely difficult, and current methods often rely on theoretical assumptions that may not hold in practice. In this paper, we introduce a new class of Nash equilibrium prediction models called Nash Fixed Point Networks (N-FPNs). N-FPNs are designed to be more robust and accurate in predicting the equilibrium of a game by using a novel architecture that is based on fixed point theory. N-FPNs are shown to be more effective than traditional models in a variety of settings, including games with continuous and discrete variables, and are able to handle complex and high-dimensional games.

This study introduces a novel method for reducing the dimensionality of high-dimensional outcome variables in the context of average causal effects. The proposed method, which is a two-stage approach, involves initially applying dimensionality reduction techniques to the outcomes and subsequently estimating the average causal effects using the reduced dimensions. The method's effectiveness is evaluated through a comprehensive simulation study, which demonstrates that the bias resulting from the initial dimensionality reduction can be counterbalanced by the reduction in estimation variance. Consequently, the findings suggest that the choice of dimensionality reduction technique should be guided by the anticipated magnitude of bias rather than solely by the minimization of estimation variance.

This research focuses on detecting stealthy attacks in cyber-physical systems that utilize a Kalman filter for anomaly detection. The detection method relies on monitoring the attack's impact on the system's state and comparing it to the system's actual behavior. The proposed approach is designed to work in real-time by using online monitoring techniques. The results show that the new method is effective in identifying attacks with lower false alarm rates and a wider range of detectable attacks.

This paper presents a novel Graph Autoencoder model with Information Sampling, known as GAE-ISumm, to efficiently summarize lengthy documents. By modeling a document as a graph, where each word is a node and relationships are captured through co-occurrence, GAE-ISumm effectively captures the semantic connections between words. To efficiently summarize, it employs Information Sampling, a technique that generates a condensed graph representing the document's key information. The resulting graph is then used to produce a summary, with the performance of GAE-ISumm surpassing that of existing state-of-the-art models on the CNN/DailyMail dataset.

A future instrument, known as MICADO, is designed to be a highly sensitive, high-resolution imaging device for the Extremely Large Telescope.  It is specifically tailored to detect and characterize exoplanets in the vicinity of nearby stars. This paper investigates the underlying principles of the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) by examining its objective function. We demonstrate that VAE optimizes a balance between two key components: the likelihood of observed data and the compactness of the latent space. To achieve this, we develop a novel theoretical framework that expresses the VAE objective function in terms of the entropy of the latent space and the KL-divergence between the encoder's output and the prior distribution. This framework enables us to derive a novel variational lower bound for the compactness of the latent space. We also provide a theoretical explanation for the well-known VAE pitfall known as the VAE collapse, and suggest a new approach to mitigate this issue.

This research paper presents a novel method for localizing smart home devices using WiFi signals. The method involves using the distance between a device and multiple WiFi routers to determine its location. A dataset of 1000 device positions was collected, along with corresponding distance and signal strength data. A machine learning model was developed to predict device locations based on this data, achieving a high level of accuracy. The model's performance was evaluated using various metrics, including the average distance between predicted and actual device locations. The results show that the proposed method is effective and can be used in real-world smart home applications.

This paper presents a new approach to multi-view representation learning that leverages deep autoencoders. The proposed method utilizes a novel quantization technique to efficiently capture the underlying structure of complex data sets. The results demonstrate that the developed framework outperforms existing maximum mutual information quantization methods and achieves comparable performance to other state-of-the-art techniques.

This study investigates parameterized algorithms for directed acyclic graphs with respect to the tree width of their transitive closures. The initial algorithm developed for this problem had a running time of $f(k)n^{O(k)}$, but it was based on an unoptimized approach. In contrast, a new algorithm has been developed with an improved running time of $f(k)n^{O(k)}$ by utilizing an unoptimized approach. This algorithm can be adapted to solve various problems, such as finding the longest path or determining the $k$-th longest path in a DAG. The algorithm's efficiency is demonstrated by comparing it to existing methods, which had a running time of $f(k)n^{O(k)}$ for similar problems. The new algorithm's efficiency is further demonstrated by its ability to solve the $k$-th longest path problem with a running time of $f(k)n^{O(k)}$. A widely used method for handling uncertain labeling in machine learning involves ensemble modeling, where multiple neural networks are trained and their outputs are combined to improve accuracy. However, the underlying reasons for the success of this approach are not fully understood. In this research, we investigate the effectiveness of ensemble methods in the presence of noisy labels, focusing on how these methods compare to a single, well-trained model. Our findings indicate that, under certain conditions, an ensemble model can achieve better results than a single model, even when the data is corrupted with noise. Moreover, we demonstrate that, in some cases, ensemble methods can achieve a better trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency, making them a promising approach for a variety of machine learning tasks.

This research develops new methods for analyzing the correlation decay properties of special semiflows in two-dimensional spaces. We demonstrate that certain transfer operators associated with both uniformly and nonuniformly expanding semiflows belong to specific functional classes, allowing us to derive precise estimates for their spectral properties. These findings are applied to establish the validity of the central limit theorem for a wide range of observables in nonuniformly expanding semiflows.

A covering array is said to be k-uniform if its size matches the product of its dimensions divided by the product of the first k integers. A modified version of this concept, known as the general covering array, allows for some flexibility in its size by adding a small margin of error. Researchers have recently found that general covering arrays can be significantly smaller than their uniform counterparts. In this study, we investigate the relationship between general and uniform covering arrays, specifically by establishing a connection between them through a specific inequality involving the dimensions and parameters of the arrays.
